_why: Rows for tests/test_filter_compiler_rows_live.py (C4, rule 16): the OLD and the NEW
predicate for every golden case (tests/fixtures/filter_compile_golden.json) must select
the same ids over these rows, and every regular single-filter case must select a
strict, non-empty subset of the grain's invariant cohort - so a test that compares
two empty sets cannot pass for the wrong reason.
listings grain (the comparables, velocity and corridor cohort); `properties_public`
seeds the Watchdog grain. Keys a seeded relation does not have are annotations, not
columns: `price_per_m2` and `plot_area_m2` on a listings row are what
measure_price_per_m2() / plot_area_m2() return for it (the live test asserts that),
and the golden takes each bound's median from them. `<col>__days_ago` seeds
`<col> = now() - N days`; `lat`/`lng` on a listing_location row seed its geom.
Deliberate edge rows: NULLs in every filtered column, a zero in every bounded one, the
non-canonical furnished/ownership value 'neuvedeno', every building_type bucket, a
listing with no point (39) and two outside the radius (37, 38), a given-up fetch
failure (36), a non-canonical advert (7, the subject, whose canonical sibling is 20),
an unresolved (1040) and a foreign (1039) Watchdog row, and a land sale at 0 CZK on each
